subject: Integration & Dedicated: embedding/rerank architecture + queue/autoscale next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fintegrate.com>, Adam Cho <adam@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Jan 2028 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: embedding + rerank design and dedicated capacity questions

Thanks for the time today — really helpful walkthrough of Fintegrate's search+recommendation flow. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope Dedicated properly: 

Summary of what we heard from your side:
- Query mix: 60% short direct queries (<= 50 tokens) and 40% rich queries that trigger embeddings + reranker (avg 450 tokens).
- Peak traffic: ~120 qps peak (12:00-14:00 PST window). Baseline steady-state: ~45 qps.
- Reranker workflow: candidate generation via sparse index -> top-100 candidates -> embedding similarity -> neural reranker scoring. Embedding calls are batched (you currently do batch size 32) but latency-sensitive rerank stage needs < 300ms p99.
- Auth & infra: you prefer mTLS for inter-service calls and want a short-lived token for user-to-backend calls (OIDC flow).

Our immediate engineering asks (items for the scoping workshop):
1) SDK & auth: a) Confirm whether you can accept server-side API keys or need mutual TLS for all calls originating from your services. b) Any existing IAM provider (Okta/Azure AD)? c) Will you proxy requests through an API gateway?
2) Routing & fallbacks: define acceptable fallback behavior when Dedicated is saturated (e.g., 1) degrade to smaller quantized model, 2) route to hosted fallback region, or 3) queue with TTL). We suggest a two-tier fallback: small quantized model then queue.
3) Embeddings and reranker sizing: a) Expected number of embedding vectors per second at peak, b) Candidate set sizes that go to the neural reranker, c) whether you can tolerate async rerank for lower-priority requests.
4) Queues & concurrency: define concurrency limits at request and token level. We generally recommend request concurrency of ~200 per-GPU for chat/small models, but embedding/rerank workloads often need dedicated GPU worker pools and bounded queue depths.

Proposed next steps: 
- Engineering workshop (1.5 hrs) to review traffic CSV + run a quick load profile.
- Draft Dedicated sizing proposal (we'll bring a baseline config: 4 x A100-equivalent nodes, 2 warm replicas for rerank pool, burst capacity to 6 nodes).
- Security checklist: we'll send our checklist for mTLS/OIDC and log retention shortly.

Attachments: please send the traffic CSV you mentioned (sample attached in meeting). If you can also share a short list of top-queries and current batch sizes we can simulate realistic token distribution.

Thanks —
Sean

Sean — thanks for the clear note. Attaching the traffic CSV (sample window + 7-day aggregate) and a short doc listing our candidate sizes. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- We can do server-side short-lived API keys for backend-to-Redwood calls. Customer-facing requests go through our API gateway (Akana) which enforces OIDC.
- Embeddings traffic: at peak we expect ~4,800 vectors/min (roughly 80 vectors/sec) during the batch-heavy window, but reranker calls (neural scoring) are higher cost — for every query that triggers rerank we score top-32 candidates.
- Latency requirement: reranker p95 < 220ms, p99 < 400ms. For lower-priority analytics queries we can accept async rerank (batching overnight).

Can you include a concrete proposal for: the rerank pool sizing (workers per GPU), queue architecture for p99-sensitive requests, and an autoscale plan that avoids cold-start penalties?

We prefer a workshop later this week (Thu or Fri morning PST).

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: embedding + rerank design and dedicated capacity questions

Hi Elena / Adam — thanks for the data. I ran a quick back-of-envelope with the numbers you sent. Below is a proposed Dedicated topology and the operational controls we'd use. This is a working draft for the workshop.

Key inputs (from CSV):
- Peak QPS (user-facing): 120
- Embedding vectors/sec peak: ~80
- Rerank candidates per query: 32
- Avg tokens per query (for rerank path): 450 tokens

Draft Dedicated proposal:
A) Topology
- Rerank pool: 3 GPU workers (A100-equivalent) continuously warm, each capable of ~40 neural rerank requests/s at target latency (p95 180ms). This covers ~120 r/s if evenly distributed; we add 2 warm spare replicas for safety -> total 5 nodes in rerank pool.
- Embedding/generation pool: 2 nodes optimized for batching embeddings (higher batch throughput). Use larger batch windows for background/analytics.
- Front-door autoscale group: start at 2 servers for lightweight routes (short queries), scale to max 6 for peak.
- Burst capacity: enable 2-node burst (on-demand) to avoid missing peaks; policy triggers at 70% GPU utilization sustained for 30s.

B) Concurrency & queueing
- Request concurrency per GPU (neural rerank): cap at 80 concurrent requests per GPU worker (to bound memory/KV cache size).
- Token-level concurrency: limit in-flight tokens to 60k tokens/GPU to prevent OOM on long contexts.
- Queue design: priority queues with TTLs — p99-sensitive route uses a dedicated high-priority queue (short TTL 700ms) and preemption of lower-priority queue. Lower-priority rerank jobs go to an async queue with batching window 500-2000ms.

C) Fallback & routing
- Primary: if rerank pool saturated, fallback to smaller quantized reranker (approx 2x speed-up, lower-quality) for 70% of traffic; remaining requests are queued for 300ms before fallback.
- Secondary: if both pools saturated, route non-critical requests to hosted region (with notice) or return cached candidate list.

D) Autoscale knobs and warm start
- Keep a small warm pool for each critical worker (2 warm replicas) to avoid cold-starts.
- Autoscale policy based on sustained GPU util + queue depth: scale up when util > 68% for 30s OR queue depth > 200. Scale down after util < 30% for 120s and queue depth < 40.
- Pre-warm strategy for scheduled peaks (you mentioned daily peak): schedule warm-up 5 minutes ahead of predicted window.

E) Observability & SLIs
- Per-request token cost, p95/p99 latency splits for embedding and reranker stages, queue depth, worker GPU util, and rollback metrics (quantized fallback rates).

I'll prepare a visual diagram for the workshop and a sample cluster config (K8s/nomad flavors). For the workshop we should:
- Walk through the CSV live, validate candidate widths, and run a few simulated runs.
- Lock down auth flow (we can accept short-lived server API keys; mTLS would be extra and supported if you want).

Action items before workshop:
- Elena: confirm Thu 11 Jan 10:00-11:30 PST or Fri 12 Jan 09:00-10:30 PST.
- Adam: share any embargoed query patterns (e.g., bursty batch imports).
- Sean/Jasmine: we'll circulate a draft cluster config + a quick perf-sim by Wed EOD.
